elements.a: The `<a>` HTML element (or anchor element), with its `href` attribute, creates a hyperlink to web pages, files, email addresses, locations in the same page, or anything else a URL can address.
elements.address: Contact information for a page or article element
elements.area: Hyperlink or dead area on an image map
elements.base: Base URL and default target navigable for hyperlinks and forms
elements.blockquote: A section quoted from another source
elements.br: Line break, e.g. in poem or postal address
elements.button: The `<button>` HTML element is an interactive element activated by a user with a mouse, keyboard, finger, voice command, or other assistive technology. Once activated, it then performs an action, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.
elements.caption: Table caption
elements.colgroup: Group of columns in a table
elements.datalist: Container for options for combo box control
elements.div: The `<div>` HTML element is the generic container for flow content. It has no effect on the content or layout until styled in some way using CSS (e.g., styling is directly applied to it, or some kind of layout model like Flexbox is applied to its parent element).
elements.dl: Association list consisting of zero or more name-value groups
elements.footer: The `<footer>` HTML element represents a footer for its nearest ancestor sectioning content or sectioning root element. A `<footer>` typically contains information about the author of the section, copyright data or links to related documents.
elements.head: Container for document metadata
elements.header: The `<header>` HTML element represents introductory content, typically a group of introductory or navigational aids. It may contain some heading elements but also a logo, a search form, an author name, and other elements.
elements.img: The `` HTML element embeds an image into the document.
elements.input: The `<input>` HTML element is used to create interactive controls for web-based forms in order to accept data from the user; a wide variety of types of input data and control widgets are available, depending on the device and user agent. The `<input>` element is one of the most powerful and complex in all of HTML due to the sheer number of combinations of input types and attributes.
elements.label: The `<label>` HTML element represents a caption for an item in a user interface.
elements.li: The `<li>` HTML element is used to represent an item in a list. It must be contained in a parent element: an ordered list (<ol>), an unordered list (<ul>), or a menu (<menu>). In menus and unordered lists, list items are usually displayed using bullet points. In ordered lists, they are usually displayed with an ascending counter on the left, such as a number or letter.
elements.main: Container for the dominant contents of the document
elements.nav: The `<nav>` HTML element represents a section of a page whose purpose is to provide navigation links, either within the current document or to other documents. Common examples of navigation sections are menus, tables of contents, and indexes.
elements.optgroup: Group of options in a list box
elements.option: Option in a list box or combo box control
elements.p:
The `

` HTML element represents a paragraph. Paragraphs are usually represented in visual media as blocks of text separated from adjacent blocks by blank lines and/or first-line indentation, but HTML paragraphs can be any structural grouping of related content, such as images or form fields.
elements.section: The `<section>` HTML element represents a generic standalone section of a document, which doesn't have a more specific semantic element to represent it. Sections should always have a heading, with very few exceptions.
elements.select: The `<select>` HTML element represents a control that provides a menu of options.
elements.source: Image source for img or media source for video or audio
elements.span: The `<span>` HTML element is a generic inline container for phrasing content, which does not inherently represent anything. It can be used to group elements for styling purposes (using the `class` or `id` attributes), or because they share attribute values, such as `lang`. It should be used only when no other semantic element is appropriate. `<span>` is very much like a <div> element, but <div> is a block-level element whereas a `<span>` is an inline-level element.
elements.tbody: Group of rows in a table
elements.textarea: The `<textarea>` HTML element represents a multi-line plain-text editing control, useful when you want to allow users to enter a sizeable amount of free-form text, for example a comment on a review or feedback form.
elements.tfoot: Group of footer rows in a table
elements.thead: Group of heading rows in a table
elements.time: Machine-readable equivalent of date- or time-related data
elements.title: Document title
elements.ul: The `<ul>` HTML element represents an unordered list of items, typically rendered as a bulleted list.

attributes.abbr: Alternative label to use for the header cell when referencing the cell in other contexts
attributes.accept: Hint for expected file type in file upload controls
attributes.accept-charset: Character encodings to use for form submission
attributes.accesskey: Keyboard shortcut to activate or focus element
attributes.action: URL to use for form submission
attributes.allow: Permissions policy to be applied to the iframe's contents
attributes.allowfullscreen: Whether to allow the iframe's contents to use requestFullscreen()
attributes.alpha: Allow the color's alpha component to be set
attributes.alt: Defines text that can replace the image in the page.
attributes.as: Destination for a preload request (for rel="preload" and rel="modulepreload")
attributes.async: Execute script when available, without blocking while fetching
attributes.autocapitalize: Recommended autocapitalization behavior (for supported input methods)
attributes.autocomplete: Default setting for autofill feature for controls in the form
attributes.autocorrect: Recommended autocorrection behavior (for supported input methods)
attributes.autofocus: Automatically focus the element when the page is loaded
attributes.autoplay: Hint that the media resource can be started automatically when the page is loaded
attributes.blocking: Whether the element is potentially render-blocking
attributes.checked: Valid for both `radio` and `checkbox` types, `checked` is a Boolean attribute. If present on a `radio` type, it indicates that the radio button is the currently selected one in the group of same-named radio buttons. If present on a `checkbox` type, it indicates that the checkbox is checked by default (when the page loads). It does not indicate whether this checkbox is currently checked: if the checkbox's state is changed, this content attribute does not reflect the change. (Only the `HTMLInputElement`'s `checked` IDL attribute is updated.)
attributes.cite: Link to the source of the quotation or more information about the edit
attributes.class: Classes to which the element belongs
attributes.closedby: Which user actions will close the dialog
attributes.color: Color to use when customizing a site's icon (for rel="mask-icon")
attributes.colorspace: The color space of the serialized color
attributes.cols: The visible width of the text control, in average character widths. If it is specified, it must be a positive integer. If it is not specified, the default value is `20`.
attributes.colspan: Number of columns that the cell is to span
attributes.command: Indicates to the targeted element which action to take.
attributes.commandfor: Targets another element to be invoked.
attributes.coords: Coordinates for the shape to be created in an image map
attributes.crossorigin: How the element handles crossorigin requests
attributes.datetime: Date and (optionally) time of the change
attributes.decoding: Decoding hint to use when processing this image for presentation
attributes.default: Enable the track if no other text track is more suitable
attributes.dir: The text directionality of the element
attributes.dirname: Name of form control to use for sending the element's directionality in form submission
attributes.disabled: The Boolean `disabled` attribute, when present, makes the element not mutable, focusable, or even submitted with the form. The user can neither edit nor focus on the control, nor its form control descendants.
attributes.download: Causes the browser to treat the linked URL as a download. Can be used with or without a `filename` value.
attributes.enctype: Entry list encoding type to use for form submission
attributes.enterkeyhint: Hint for selecting an enter key action
attributes.fetchpriority: Sets the priority for fetches initiated by the element
attributes.for: The `for` attribute is an allowed attribute for <label> and <output>. When used on a `<label>` element it indicates the form element that this label describes. When used on an `<output>` element it allows for an explicit relationship between the elements that represent values which are used in the output.
attributes.form: Associates the element with a form element
attributes.formaction: URL to use for form submission
attributes.formenctype: Entry list encoding type to use for form submission
attributes.formmethod: Variant to use for form submission
attributes.formnovalidate: Bypass form control validation for form submission
attributes.headers: The header cells for this cell
attributes.headingreset: Prevents a heading offset computation from traversing beyond the element with the attribute
attributes.height: The intrinsic height of the image, in pixels. Must be an integer without a unit.
attributes.href: The URL that the hyperlink points to. Links are not restricted to HTTP-based URLs — they can use any URL scheme supported by browsers.
attributes.imagesizes: Image sizes for different page layouts (for rel="preload")
attributes.imagesrcset: Images to use in different situations, e.g., high-resolution displays, small monitors, etc. (for rel="preload")
attributes.inputmode: Hint for selecting an input modality
attributes.integrity: Integrity metadata used in Subresource Integrity checks [SRI]
attributes.ismap: Whether the image is a server-side image map
attributes.itemid: Global identifier for a microdata item
attributes.itemprop: Property names of a microdata item
attributes.itemtype: Item types of a microdata item
attributes.label: User-visible label
attributes.loop: Whether to loop the media resource
attributes.max: The `max` attribute defines the maximum value that is acceptable and valid for the input containing the attribute. If the `value` of the element is greater than this, the element fails validation. This value must be greater than or equal to the value of the `min` attribute. If the `max` attribute is present but is not specified or is invalid, no `max` value is applied. If the `max` attribute is valid and a non-empty value is greater than the maximum allowed by the `max` attribute, constraint validation will prevent form submission.
attributes.method: Variant to use for form submission
attributes.min: The `min` attribute defines the minimum value that is acceptable and valid for the input containing the attribute. If the `value` of the element is less than this, the element fails validation. This value must be less than or equal to the value of the `max` attribute.
attributes.multiple: The Boolean `multiple` attribute, if set, means the form control accepts one or more values. The attribute is valid for the email and file input types and the <select>. The manner by which the user opts for multiple values depends on the form control.
attributes.muted: Whether to mute the media resource by default
attributes.name: A string specifying a name for the input control. This name is submitted along with the control's value when the form data is submitted.
attributes.nomodule: Prevents execution in user agents that support module scripts
attributes.nonce: Cryptographic nonce used in Content Security Policy checks [CSP]
attributes.novalidate: Bypass form control validation for form submission
attributes.pattern: Pattern to be matched by the form control's value
attributes.placeholder: The `placeholder` attribute defines the text displayed in a form control when the control has no value. The placeholder text should provide a brief hint to the user as to the expected type of data that should be entered into the control.
attributes.playsinline: Encourage the user agent to display video content within the element's playback area
attributes.popover: Makes the element a popover element
attributes.popovertarget: Targets a popover element to toggle, show, or hide
attributes.popovertargetaction: Indicates whether a targeted popover element is to be toggled, shown, or hidden
attributes.poster: Poster frame to show prior to video playback
attributes.preload: Hints how much buffering the media resource will likely need
attributes.readonly: The Boolean `readonly` attribute, when present, makes the element not mutable, meaning the user can not edit the control.
attributes.referrerpolicy: Referrer policy for fetches initiated by the element
attributes.rel: The `rel` attribute defines the relationship between a linked resource and the current document. Valid on <link>, <a>, <area>, and <form>, the supported values depend on the element on which the attribute is found.
attributes.required: The Boolean `required` attribute, if present, indicates that the user must specify a value for the input before the owning form can be submitted.
attributes.rows: The number of visible text lines for the control. If it is specified, it must be a positive integer. If it is not specified, the default value is 2.
attributes.rowspan: Number of rows that the cell is to span
attributes.scope: Specifies which cells the header cell applies to
attributes.selected: If present, this Boolean attribute indicates that the option is initially selected. If the `<option>` element is the descendant of a <select> element whose `multiple` attribute is not set, only one single `<option>` of this <select> element may have the `selected` attribute.
attributes.shadowrootclonable: Sets clonable on a declarative shadow root
attributes.shadowrootcustomelementregistry: Enables declarative shadow roots to indicate they will use a custom element registry
attributes.shadowrootdelegatesfocus: Sets delegates focus on a declarative shadow root
attributes.shadowrootserializable: Sets serializable on a declarative shadow root
attributes.shadowrootslotassignment: Sets slot assignment on a declarative shadow root
attributes.shape: The kind of shape to be created in an image map
attributes.span: Number of columns spanned by the element
attributes.spellcheck: Whether the element is to have its spelling and grammar checked
attributes.src: The image URL. At least one of `src` and `srcset` is required for an `` element. If `srcset` is specified, `src` is used in one of two ways.
attributes.srcdoc: A document to render in the iframe
attributes.srcset: Images to use in different situations, e.g., high-resolution displays, small monitors, etc.
attributes.step: The `step` attribute is a number that specifies the granularity that the value must adhere to or the keyword `any`. It is valid for the numeric input types, including the date, month, week, time, datetime-local, number and range types.
attributes.tabindex: Whether the element is focusable and sequentially focusable, and the relative order of the element for the purposes of sequential focus navigation
attributes.target: Where to display the linked URL, as the name for a browsing context (a tab, window, or <iframe>). The following keywords have special meanings for where to load the URL.
attributes.title: Advisory information for the element
attributes.translate: Whether the element is to be translated when the page is localized
attributes.type: A string specifying the type of control to render. For example, to create a checkbox, a value of `checkbox` is used. If omitted (or an unknown value is specified), the input type `text` is used, creating a plaintext input field.
attributes.usemap: Name of image map to use
attributes.value: The input control's value. When specified in the HTML, this is the initial value, and from then on it can be altered or retrieved at any time using JavaScript to access the respective HTMLInputElement object's `value` property. The `value` attribute is always optional, though should be considered mandatory for `checkbox`, `radio`, and `hidden`.
attributes.width: The intrinsic width of the image in pixels. Must be an integer without a unit.
attributes.wrap: How the value of the form control is to be wrapped for form submission
attributes.writingsuggestions: Whether the element can offer writing suggestions or not.
attributes.onafterprint: afterprint event handler for Window object
attributes.onbeforeprint: beforeprint event handler for Window object
attributes.onbeforeunload: beforeunload event handler for Window object
attributes.onhashchange: hashchange event handler for Window object
attributes.onlanguagechange: languagechange event handler for Window object
attributes.onmessage: message event handler for Window object
attributes.onmessageerror: messageerror event handler for Window object
attributes.onoffline: offline event handler for Window object
attributes.ononline: online event handler for Window object
attributes.onpagehide: pagehide event handler for Window object
attributes.onpagereveal: pagereveal event handler for Window object
attributes.onpageshow: pageshow event handler for Window object
attributes.onpageswap: pageswap event handler for Window object
attributes.onpopstate: popstate event handler for Window object
attributes.onrejectionhandled: rejectionhandled event handler for Window object
attributes.onstorage: storage event handler for Window object
attributes.onunhandledrejection: unhandledrejection event handler for Window object
attributes.onunload: unload event handler for Window object
attributes.role: The WAI-ARIA role that defines the type of this element for assistive technologies.
attributes.aria-activedescendant: Identifies the currently active descendant of a composite widget.
attributes.aria-atomic: Whether assistive technologies present the entire changed live region as a whole.
attributes.aria-autocomplete: What kind of user-input completion suggestions the widget provides.
attributes.aria-braillelabel: A braille label overriding the accessible name for braille displays.
attributes.aria-brailleroledescription: A human-readable braille description of the element role.
attributes.aria-busy: Whether an element and its subtree are currently being updated.
attributes.aria-checked: The checked state of checkboxes, radio buttons and other toggle widgets.
attributes.aria-colcount: The total number of columns in a table, grid or treegrid.
attributes.aria-colindex: The column index of an element relative to the total number of columns.
attributes.aria-colspan: The number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell.
attributes.aria-controls: Identifies the element(s) whose contents or presence this element controls.
attributes.aria-current: The current item within a set of related elements.
attributes.aria-describedby: Identifies the element(s) that describe this element.
attributes.aria-description: A string value that describes or annotates the current element.
attributes.aria-details: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description.
attributes.aria-disabled: Whether the element is perceivable but disabled and not editable or operable.
attributes.aria-dropeffect: What functions can be performed when a dragged object is released (deprecated).
attributes.aria-errormessage: Identifies the element that provides an error message for this element.
attributes.aria-expanded: Whether a grouping element owned or controlled by this element is expanded.
attributes.aria-flowto: The next element(s) in an alternate reading order of content.
attributes.aria-grabbed: The grabbed state of an element in a drag-and-drop operation (deprecated).
attributes.aria-haspopup: Whether the element has a popup, and the type of popup it triggers.
attributes.aria-hidden: Whether the element is exposed to the accessibility API.
attributes.aria-invalid: Whether the entered value does not conform to the expected format.
attributes.aria-keyshortcuts: Keyboard shortcuts that activate or focus the element.
attributes.aria-label: A string value that labels the current element.
attributes.aria-labelledby: Identifies the element(s) that label this element.
attributes.aria-level: The hierarchical level of an element within a structure.
attributes.aria-live: How assistive technologies should announce updates to a live region.
attributes.aria-modal: Whether an element is modal when displayed.
attributes.aria-multiline: Whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input.
attributes.aria-multiselectable: Whether the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.
attributes.aria-orientation: Whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical or unknown.
attributes.aria-owns: Identifies child element(s) to define a parent/child relationship the DOM cannot.
attributes.aria-placeholder: A short hint intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
attributes.aria-posinset: An element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems.
attributes.aria-pressed: The pressed state of a toggle button.
attributes.aria-readonly: Whether the element is not editable but is otherwise operable.
attributes.aria-relevant: What notifications the user agent triggers when a live region changes.
attributes.aria-required: Whether user input is required on the element before form submission.
attributes.aria-roledescription: A human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.
attributes.aria-rowcount: The total number of rows in a table, grid or treegrid.
attributes.aria-rowindex: The row index of an element relative to the total number of rows.
attributes.aria-rowspan: The number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell.
attributes.aria-selected: The selected state of a selectable element.
attributes.aria-setsize: The number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems.
attributes.aria-sort: Whether items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.
attributes.aria-valuemax: The maximum allowed value for a range widget.
attributes.aria-valuemin: The minimum allowed value for a range widget.
attributes.aria-valuenow: The current value for a range widget.
attributes.aria-valuetext: A human-readable text alternative of the current value of a range widget.
attributes.part: Names the element so it can be targeted by the ::part() pseudo-element from outside its shadow tree.
attributes.exportparts: Re-exports named shadow parts of a nested shadow tree to the outer tree for ::part() styling.
attributes.privateToken: Configures Private State Token operations for the fetch (experimental).
attributes.attributionsrc: Registers the element as an attribution source/trigger for the Attribution Reporting API.
attributes.browsingtopics: Opts the request into the Topics API (experimental).
attributes.credentialless: Loads the iframe in a new, credentialless ephemeral context.
attributes.csp: A Content Security Policy to enforce on the framed document.
attributes.anchor: Associates the element with an anchor element for CSS anchor positioning.
attributes.virtualkeyboardpolicy: Controls whether the on-screen virtual keyboard shows automatically on focus.
attributes.interestfor: Associates the element with a target it shows interest in (experimental invoker/interest proposal).
attributes.switch: Renders the checkbox as a switch control.
attributes.shadowrootreferencetarget: The reference target id for a declarative shadow root (experimental).
attributes.webkitdirectory: Allows the file input to select entire directories (non-standard).
attributes.capture: Which camera or microphone to use when capturing media for a file input.
attributes.controlslist: Hints which native media controls the user agent should hide (nodownload, nofullscreen, noremoteplayback).
attributes.disablepictureinpicture: Disables the Picture-in-Picture feature for the video element.
attributes.disableremoteplayback: Disables remote-playback (casting) for the media element.
attributes.hreftranslate: A BCP 47 language tag hinting the preferred translation language of the linked resource.
attributes.xmlns: The XML namespace of the root element (only meaningful in XML/XHTML serialization).
attributes.align: Deprecated presentational alignment of the element; use CSS instead.
attributes.alink: Deprecated color of active hyperlinks in the document; use CSS instead.
attributes.allowpaymentrequest: Obsolete: allowed the iframe to use the Payment Request API.
attributes.archive: Obsolete: space-separated list of archive URLs for an applet/object.
attributes.axis: Obsolete: named the category of a table cell for header association.
attributes.background: Deprecated URL of a background image for the element; use CSS instead.
attributes.bgcolor: Deprecated background color of the element; use CSS instead.
attributes.border: Deprecated width of the border around a table or image; use CSS instead.
attributes.bottommargin: Deprecated bottom margin of the document body; use CSS instead.
attributes.cellpadding: Deprecated padding inside table cells; use CSS instead.
attributes.cellspacing: Deprecated spacing between table cells; use CSS instead.
attributes.char: Obsolete: the alignment character for a table column.
attributes.charoff: Obsolete: offset of column data from the alignment character.
attributes.classid: Obsolete: URL identifying the implementation of an object.
attributes.clear: Deprecated: controlled float clearing on a line break; use CSS instead.
attributes.codebase: Obsolete: base URL for resolving an object/applet relative URLs.
attributes.codetype: Obsolete: expected MIME type of the object code identified by classid.
attributes.compact: Deprecated: requested a compact rendering of a list; use CSS instead.
attributes.declare: Obsolete: declared an object without instantiating it.
attributes.frame: Deprecated: which outer borders of a table are drawn; use CSS instead.
attributes.frameborder: Deprecated: whether to draw a border around a frame/iframe; use CSS instead.
attributes.hspace: Deprecated: horizontal whitespace around the element; use CSS instead.
attributes.leftmargin: Deprecated left margin of the document body; use CSS instead.
attributes.link: Deprecated color of unvisited hyperlinks in the document; use CSS instead.
attributes.longdesc: Obsolete: URL of a long description of an image or frame.
attributes.marginheight: Deprecated top/bottom margin of a frame; use CSS instead.
attributes.marginwidth: Deprecated left/right margin of a frame; use CSS instead.
attributes.nohref: Obsolete: marked an image-map area as having no associated hyperlink.
attributes.noshade: Deprecated: rendered a horizontal rule without shading; use CSS instead.
attributes.rev: Obsolete: reverse link relationship from the linked resource to the current document.
attributes.rightmargin: Deprecated right margin of the document body; use CSS instead.
attributes.rules: Deprecated: which inner borders of a table are drawn; use CSS instead.
attributes.scheme: Obsolete: named the profile/scheme used to interpret a meta value.
attributes.scrolling: Deprecated: whether a frame provides scrollbars; use CSS instead.
attributes.standby: Obsolete: message shown while an object loads.
attributes.summary: Obsolete on table: a text description of the table for accessibility; use a caption instead.
attributes.text: Deprecated foreground text color of the document body; use CSS instead.
attributes.topmargin: Deprecated top margin of the document body; use CSS instead.
attributes.valign: Deprecated vertical alignment of table cell content; use CSS instead.
attributes.version: Obsolete: the HTML DTD version of the document.
attributes.vlink: Deprecated color of visited hyperlinks in the document; use CSS instead.
attributes.vspace: Deprecated: vertical whitespace around the element; use CSS instead.
